newsitem.title: UK: FTSE seen showing restraint in tracking Dow.
newsitem.headline: FTSE seen showing restraint in tracking Dow.

text.p: A further rally by the Dow could lead the London stock market even higher into record territory next week but strategists say its gains will continue to lag those in U.S. shares because of a less favourable domestic economic and political outlook.

London's blue-chip FTSE 100 share index surged to an all-time high of 4,353.4 on Friday, inspired by a third day of sharp gains in the U.S. market on Thursday, which took the Dow Jones idustrial average above the 7,000 landmark for the first time.
But so far this year the Dow has almost doubled the advance seen on the FTSE 100, which has risen by 5-1/2 percent since January, compared with the Dow's nine percent surge.
Economists say domestic worries are increasingly restraining the London market.
The proximity to a general election, persistent strength of sterling, a weakening corporate earnings trend and the inflation and interest rate environment have all dulled investors' appetites.
Meanwhile, the Dow has risen by more than 1,000 points in just four months, adding 216 points in the last three days alone, amid growing optimism over the U.S. economy.
Steady inflation, strong corporate profits, low interest rates and a strong dollar have all helped to boost Wall Street.
British equities have fewer incentives to justify the current demanding valuation of the market.
"The background of a weakening earnings trend has really distinguished us from the U.S. and particularly the rest of Europe," said Paul O'Connor, equities strategist at BZW.
"We're not particularly upbeat about the FTSE from here," he added, commenting that his year-end forecast for the index remains at 4,300.
"Looking ahead we have political uncertainty and valuations are still stretched.

"The real key that could change our outlook would be a big change in policy mix after the election," said O'Connor. "A tightening of policy will help gilts, take the heat off short rates and sterling and also help company earnings."
Investors are also increasingly aware of recent wide swings in the U.S. stock market and fear that a sudden turnaround in sentiment could have a big impact on British stocks.
"With the Dow looking so strong at the moment, we can't rule out further upside in the FTSE," said Richard Jeffrey, head of research at Charterhouse Tilney.
"But having said that, I think the Dow is approaching the top of its justifiable valuation range, the upside is very limited now and it might even be entering dangerous territory.
"I think in London we have to start being very wary about the implications of the Dow moving much higher."
Scheduled economic news on British retail sales and U.S consumer prices next Wednesday will help provide a focus for investors, giving fresh evidence of how both economies are faring.
Elsewhere, analysts will be looking closely at British company results to see how persistent strength in sterling is affecting companies' earnings outlooks.
Among the FTSE 100 companies reporting results next week are Barclays Bank and SmithKline Beecham on Tuesday and BOC Group and Rank Group on Thursday.
